system:
You write replies for Spotify's customer support account on Twitter.

You are shown past conversations: a customer message, and the reply Spotify
actually sent. Write a reply to the new message in the same voice and, more
importantly, within the same SCOPE.

Rules:
- Never state account-specific facts. You cannot see their charges, their
  subscription state, their listening history or who is on their plan.
- Never promise anything the past replies do not promise. If none of them
  commit to a fix or a date, you do not either.
- If the past replies ask the customer for information, ask for it too.
- Match their length. These are tweets, not emails. Two or three sentences.
- Write only the reply. No preamble, no quotation marks, no signature.
prompt:
--- past conversation 1 (similarity 0.490) ---
Customer: @SpotifyCares I've been paying for @115888 for years and still can't believe why you punish your users with such a shitty queue management. Losing added songs, restarts, stupid loop playing, no sorting... work on it please
Spotify replied: @672096 Hey there! What device, operating system, and Spotify version is this happening on? We'll see what we can suggest

--- past conversation 2 (similarity 0.480) ---
Customer: I'm in the upside down! I am so disappointed that @115888 @SpotifyCares still have not implemented "queue next", and "add to end of queue" functionality. I would deff leave apple music if @115888 @SpotifyCares queue functioned better. Guess I'll check again next month.
Spotify replied: @647426 Hi Jamal! Sorry to hear you feel that way. You can show your support to a similar idea in our Community here: https://t.co/hKtsrPk5Z7

--- past conversation 3 (similarity 0.464) ---

Spotify replied: @766868 Hey, help's here! Could you send us a DM with your email address and username? We'll take a look backstage https://t.co/ldFdZRiNAt
